skill.name: slideshow
skill.description: Create runnable HyperFrames slideshow decks with discrete slides, fragments, branches, hotspots, presenter mode, and speaker notes. Convert existing pages into deck experiences while preserving source visuals and media behavior.
skill.summary: Build interactive HyperFrames slideshow decks with presenter mode, notes, branches, fragments, and validation guidance.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: The high static score is driven almost entirely by Markdown backticks, JavaScript template literals, and benign wording in documentation. One low-risk issue remains: an optional Three.js example imports executable code from a third-party CDN at runtime.

remediation.issue: The standalone harness references Three.js from jsdelivr.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor Three.js locally or use a package-managed build with integrity controls for generated decks.

content.value_statement: Teams need runnable decks that support navigation, notes, media, and branching. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to build validated HyperFrames slideshow projects.
actual_capabilities: Creates HyperFrames deck structures with scenes mapped to slideshow slides.
Defines slide order, fragments, branch sequences, hotspots, and speaker notes.
Guides wrapping decks with the HyperFrames slideshow component and presenter mode.
Explains media cleanup, global mute behavior, and presenter audience synchronization.
Provides lint and validation steps for completed slideshow projects.
limitations: It does not render a complete slideshow to a single MP4.
Engine-hosted slideshow preview is described as future functionality.
Standalone demos may need duplicated manifest data until engine hosting is available.
It depends on HyperFrames project conventions and available player bundles.

best_practices: Confirm the user wants a HyperFrames slideshow before authoring adjacent presentation requests.
Keep the slideshow manifest close to the scene definitions and validate every scene reference.
Run lint and runtime validation before handoff, then provide the presenter URL.
anti_patterns: Rendering the deck as one MP4 when the user needs live navigation.
Adding custom presenter buttons or note editors instead of shared slideshow controls.
Cropping screenshots, product UI, charts, or readable evidence as decorative media.

faq.question: Does this skill create a video file?
faq.answer: No. It creates a runnable HyperFrames slideshow with navigation, notes, branches, and presenter mode.

faq.question: Can it convert an existing web page?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides conversion while preserving visual design, motion, media behavior, and important interactions.

faq.question: Does it support speaker notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the shared presenter view and editable notes behavior from the slideshow player.

faq.question: Can slides include branches?
faq.answer: Yes. Hotspots can open separate slide sequences that return to the main deck.

faq.question: What validation should run before handoff?
faq.answer: Run HyperFrames lint and runtime validation. Fix scene, fragment, hotspot, and media timing issues before delivery.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
